findings.failing_input: All three cron functions set `retries: 3` (line 51, 69, 103). On a transient WhatsApp API outage at 12:00 IL, the noon summary will retry up to 3 times with Inngest's exponential backoff. Per Inngest defaults the backoff is exponential starting at ~30 sec — total retry envelope is ~5-10 min. If WhatsApp is down for ALL retries, the message is dropped silently (no operator alert for the WhatsApp summary itself).
findings.expected: Either lower the retry count to 1 (fail-fast — operator gets a deadletter signal in the Inngest dashboard sooner) or wire a notifyTokenFailure call on final failure (analogous to the WhatsApp token-failure infrastructure mentioned in PROJECT.md). Current behavior accepts silent message-drop on multi-retry failure.
findings.actual: Documented operator behavior is 'WhatsApp summaries ONLY to +972524809540' (per memory project_token_failure_alerts_pending). The operator IS the recipient — if WhatsApp is down for the operator's number, the operator wouldn't get a 'WhatsApp failed' WhatsApp anyway. Best path is the in-dashboard Inngest deadletter signal (which the operator monitors). Current code is fine if the operator monitors the Inngest dashboard.
findings.fix_sketch: Add an inline comment documenting 'WhatsApp transport failure → Inngest deadletter; operator-monitored via the Inngest Cloud UI; no recursive WhatsApp alert needed (alert path would itself fail).' No code change required.

findings.failing_input: The operator-triggered 'Send test' button (line 128-147) has `retries: 0` (line 132). If WhatsApp is down at the moment the operator clicks the button, the send fails permanently with no retry — operator sees an immediate failure but no signal of WHY (the catch is inside the function, the rejection bubbles to Inngest's deadletter).
findings.expected: retries:0 is intentional ('operator wants immediate feedback, not a 5-min retry storm'). Documented as such in the inline comment at line 125-127 implicitly. Acceptable.

findings.failing_input:
The inline audit comment at line 84-95 documents: cron-daily fires at 00:05 IL, has 4 retries × exponential backoff = ~7.5 min envelope worst case = finish by ~00:12.5. EOD WhatsApp fires at 00:30 IL = 25-min runway. This is well-clear.

BUT: cron-daily contains a `persist-batch` step that does ~8 sequential Supabase UPSERTs (data_daily, products_daily, 3× campaigns_daily for meta/google/tiktok, ads_daily, orders_attribution, product_catalog). At operator scale (~250 products × 3 stores), this can take 30-60s. The 5-min wall-clock step budget plus 4 retries means worst-case finish is closer to 00:30 — exactly when whatsappEod fires.

Production shape: cron-daily fires at 00:05; if Meta API has a 3-min latency spike (not uncommon for the /insights endpoint), each retry adds ~3 min + backoff. 4 retries × (3 min API + 1 min backoff) = 16 min retry envelope. Plus 1 min for the first attempt = 17 min. cron-daily finishes ~00:22 IL. whatsappEod fires at 00:30 IL → 8-min cushion, not 25-min.
findings.expected: Either widen the cushion to 1 hour (00:30 → 01:00 IL) for robust margin, OR have whatsappEod check the actual job state of cron-daily (e.g. `step.waitForEvent('cron-daily-completed-{date}', timeout: 30min)` then send).
findings.actual: The 25-min runway claim in the comment assumes cron-daily's worst-case finish is 00:12.5. That's the case if every retry is the MINIMUM backoff (~30s) and each attempt takes ~30s. Real-world API latency spikes can extend the worst-case finish to closer to 00:25-00:30.
findings.fix_sketch: Either move whatsappEod to 01:00 IL (operator only sees the EOD summary at breakfast anyway), or add a guard inside the handler that re-queries data_daily for yesterday and waits up to 30 min if the row hasn't landed yet.
findings.regression_test_idea: Production-shape simulation: assume cron-daily takes 17 min worst-case. Pin: whatsappEod fires at 00:30 IL → only 13-min cushion (not 25). Document this in the inline comment OR widen the cron expression.

uncertainty_notes: INN-13 is the highest-confidence concern but is a soft-edged claim — it depends on the actual production API latency distribution, which I don't have access to. The audit fix from 00:10 → 00:30 was a real improvement; the question is whether 00:30 is sufficient or if 01:00 would be safer. The operator's behavior 'WhatsApp ONLY to +972524809540' (per memory) is respected throughout (no recipient logic in this file — recipients are owned by sendDailySummary in @/lib/notifications/sendDailySummary). All cron expressions are TZ=Asia/Jerusalem prefixed (DST-safe per RESEARCH §Pitfall 1). All three cron functions use sendDailySummary as the single sink → if WhatsApp delivery semantics need to change, one upstream module owns it.

test_coverage_gaps.description: No test asserting `sendDailySummary` is called with the right date string for each cron variant. The unit test at cronWhatsapp.test.ts pins cron expressions + function IDs but NOT the handler body's date computation (yesterdayJerusalem for EOD vs todayJerusalem for noon/evening).
test_coverage_gaps.why_it_matters: A regression that swapped the two date helpers would silently send 'yesterday's totals' at noon (showing $0 because yesterday's data is fully written but the summary title says 'today') or 'today's partial totals' as the EOD summary (operator sees the wrong number).
test_coverage_gaps.suggested_fixture: Mock sendDailySummary; invoke each handler's step.run callback; assert the date arg passed to sendDailySummary matches todayJerusalem() (noon, evening) vs yesterdayJerusalem() (EOD).

test_coverage_gaps.description: No test for the eventWhatsappSendNow handler's trigger-switch logic (line 136-146). The 3 branches (noon / evening / eod) each compute a different date+title. A swap would silently send the wrong summary type.
test_coverage_gaps.why_it_matters: Operator's 'Send test' button is the live verification path for the WhatsApp pipeline. If the operator clicks 'send test (eod)' but the handler runs noon logic, the operator's verification is meaningless.
test_coverage_gaps.suggested_fixture: Mock sendDailySummary; invoke handler with each of the 3 trigger values; assert the (dateStr, title) tuple matches.

test_coverage_gaps.description: No test for the default `trigger ?? 'noon'` (line 136). If event.data is undefined or trigger is missing, the handler should default to noon.
test_coverage_gaps.why_it_matters: An operator-console regression that fails to set the trigger field would silently default to noon. The current default is benign (noon-summary is always meaningful) but a future change to require explicit trigger would be silently bypassed.
test_coverage_gaps.suggested_fixture: Invoke handler with event={} (no data); assert sendDailySummary called with todayJerusalem() + titleNoon.
